adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:265 — Making .small-action a flex row leaves .small-action-desc shrink-to-fit with no flex-grow, so the float:right edit/delete buttons (line 309) now sit right after the short action text instead of at the right edge of the post column.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.small-action` to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`). In a flex formatting context, floated elements inside the flex container (or floats applied to flex items) no longer behave like they did in block layout; additionally `.small-action-desc` has no flex-grow (`flex: 1` / similar) so it can size to its contents. This makes it plausible/likely that any right-floated edit/delete controls associated with the action description will no longer be pushed to the far right edge and instead appear immediately after the text or as an adjacent flex item, matching the finding’s described regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic.scss:30 — .extra-info-wrapper becomes a flex item with the default min-width:auto and no flex-shrink/overflow rule, so a long docked topic title or nowrap category badge cannot shrink below its content width and pushes .panel past the header edge or squeezes it until the floated icons wrap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff converts the header layout from floats to flex: `.contents` now `@include flexbox()`/`@include align-items(center)` (header.scss) and `.panel` is positioned via `margin-left: auto` plus `@include order(3)`. In `topic.scss`, `.extra-info-wrapper` gains `@include order(2)`, implying it is intended to participate as a flex item in that flex header row. No flex sizing constraints (e.g., `min-width: 0`, `flex-shrink`, or `overflow`) are added for `.extra-info-wrapper`, so under standard flexbox behavior it will keep `min-width:auto` and may refuse to shrink below its content width, which can push/squeeze the right-side `.panel` in long/nowrap-content cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:37 — Right-aligning .panel now depends only on margin-left:auto, which the legacy display:-webkit-box model this mixin emits does not honor, so on -webkit-box-only browsers (iOS 6, Android 4.x stock) the panel packs next to the logo instead of on the right.

adjudication.rationale: In header.scss, `.contents` was changed to use `@include flexbox()` and `.panel` lost `float: right` in favor of `margin-left: auto` (plus `@include order(3)`). The `flexbox()` mixin emits legacy `display: -webkit-box` first, which is the only recognized flex-like display in older WebKit. In that legacy box model, `margin-left: auto` is not a reliable/right way to push an item to the end (the usual mechanism is `-webkit-box-pack`/flex). So on browsers that only support `-webkit-box`, the `.panel` may no longer right-align, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:265 — align-items:center vertically centers the action icon against the whole .small-action-desc, so small actions that have a custom-message (15px top margin plus paragraphs) show the icon beside the message body instead of the action line.

With flexbox, `align-items: center` vertically centers all immediate children (e.g., `.topic-avatar`/icon) relative to the tallest child. If `.small-action-desc` becomes taller due to multi-line/custom message content, the icon/avatar will be centered alongside the block rather than aligning with the first/action line—this is a plausible visual regression introduced by the new alignment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:118 — The align-items mixin passes its value unchanged to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, which require start/end rather than flex-start/flex-end, so any future caller using those values silently gets no legacy alignment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` that forwards `$alignment` directly into legacy properties `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` (see `mixins.scss`), but those legacy syntaxes expect values like `start`/`end` rather than modern `flex-start`/`flex-end`. This means the mixin can silently fail for common align-items values, making the mixin’s cross-browser behavior incorrect as added in this PR (even though current callers in the diff use `center`/`baseline`, which happen to work).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:102 — The flexbox mixin emits display:-moz-box but the align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so legacy -moz-box renderers fall back to stretch and the header and small-action are not vertically centered.

adjudication.rationale: In mixins.scss the new `@mixin flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box;` (legacy Firefox flexbox), but the new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` does not emit the corresponding legacy property `-moz-box-align`. The diff also changes `.contents` and `.small-action` to use `@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`, so on a renderer that actually uses the `-moz-box` display mode, vertical centering/baseline alignment won’t be applied as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:35 — .panel has no flex-shrink:0, so when the logo plus panel exceed the header width (for example a wide logo on narrow mobile screens) the panel shrinks to its min-content and its floated login buttons/icons wrap onto extra rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is changed to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`). `.panel` becomes a flex item (float removed) with `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)`, but no `flex-shrink: 0` (default is `flex-shrink: 1`). Under flex layout, this allows the `.panel` to shrink when space is constrained (e.g., wide logo/narrow viewport), which can force its internal contents (e.g., login buttons/icons) to wrap within the panel. This is a plausible regression introduced by switching from floats to flexbox without constraining shrink behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117 — flexbox mixin emits display:-moz-box but align-items mixin has no -moz-box-align, so in engines that fall back to -moz-box, items stretch instead of centering and align inconsistently with the order mixin, which does emit -moz-box-ordinal-group.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:102 — The mixins hand-write obsolete 2009/2011 prefixes (`-moz-box`, `-moz-inline-box`, `-webkit-box`, `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) that nothing needs, and their semantics differ from modern flexbox.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new flexbox-related mixins in `mixins.scss` that explicitly emit legacy 2009-era properties like `display: -webkit-box`, `display: -moz-box`, `display: -webkit-inline-box`, and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` / `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (e.g., in `@mixin flexbox`, `@mixin inline-flex`, and `@mixin order`). These are indeed obsolete prefixes tied to older flexbox specs and can behave differently from modern `flex`/`order`. While the claim that “nothing needs” them can’t be proven from the diff alone, the presence of these legacy properties and potential semantic mismatch is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern rather than a directly verifiable functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117 — align-items`/`order` pass the modern value straight into the legacy `-webkit-box-align`, `-ms-flex-align` and `box-ordinal-group` properties, which use different value sets (e.g. `flex-start`) and indexing, so the mixin breaks for other inputs.

adjudication.rationale: The new mixins in `app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss` forward `$alignment` and `$val` directly into legacy flexbox properties (`-webkit-box-align`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, etc.). Those legacy properties don’t accept the same value set/indexing as modern flexbox (e.g., `-webkit-box-align` expects `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`, and `box-ordinal-group` is effectively 1-based). As written, the mixins will produce invalid/incorrect CSS for some reasonable inputs (e.g. `align-items(flex-start)` or `order(0)`), so the cross-browser intent of these mixins is broken.
